title: Can the attacker take the stage from a retreating Fox for free?
summary: Running. First results: mid-stage the defender is not forced back within 8 frames, and at the ledge the attacker has a small edge once falling off the stage counts.
plan: For a grid of starting positions (attacker standing, walking in or dashing in; 15 distances; mid-stage and six distances from the ledge) find which defender inputs are safe for 8 frames against an attacker who sees each input first. Then solve the real one-frame-late game at the positions where none is safe.

details.label: Positions searched
details.value: about 1.1 billion (90 of 630 grid jobs, 4 exact solves)

details.label: Result so far
details.value: no forced win; a small attacker edge at the ledge

findings: Proven, 8 frames, mid-stage: against a Fox walking in at 13.5 to 14.1 the only safe inputs are steps away; from 14.7 out the defender may also stand still.
Proven, 8 frames, mid-stage: with both standing 11.5 to 12.1 apart the defender has no safe input and has to guess.
Proven, 8 frames, mid-stage: stepping away costs under 3 units, so the defender is not pushed back within this lookahead.
Proven, 8 frames, at the ledge, both standing 10.3 apart: attacker's clean first hits minus defender's is 0 if falling off costs nothing, and +0.27 if leaving the stage loses the exchange.
Proven, 8 frames, at the ledge, attacker walking in at 13.9: +0.08 for the attacker with the same rule.
